meta.title: The Nat prelude, and what stands on it
meta.subtitle: One connected component of the fact ledger, rendered. Every badge, statement, hash and replay command on this page was read out of `artifacts/facts/` at build time; only the narrative was written by a person.
meta.footer_note: Rendered by `render/src/emit_html.rs`. Regenerate with the command in the document header, then `cargo test --features html -- preview`.

Prose.text:
A rendered document here is a checker output, not prose about one. That distinction is the whole design, and it is visible on this page: nothing below carries a green badge because a person decided it deserved one. Each badge is the `epistemic_status` field of a file in `artifacts/facts/`, each replay command is that file's `checker_command`, and a claim that arrived without evidence renders saying so.

What follows is one connected component of the ledger's dependency graph -- the naturals, the integers, the rationals built over them, and Euclid's theorem at the bottom of the chain -- with two deliberately unrelated facts alongside it for contrast. Read it at *summary* to see only the argument, at *full* for the evidence, at *forensic* for everything the ledger carries.

DepGraph.caption: **The prelude component.** An edge runs from a prerequisite to the result that uses it, so everything a node rests on is what sits above it. The four nodes with cards below link to them. Layered in Rust -- longest-path ranking, median sweeps, isotonic coordinates -- and drawn as inline SVG; no graph library is involved, and none could be, since the page may not fetch one.

Prose.heading: Four facts, four kinds of standing
Prose.text: The ledger keeps two status axes on purpose: what *this system* established, and what mathematics knows. They are different questions, and their disagreement in our favour is a result rather than a bookkeeping error. The four cards below are one of each interesting case.

Claim.label: There is no largest prime
Claim.statement: For every natural number n there is a prime p with n < p. Equivalently, there are infinitely many primes.

evidence.supports: For every natural number n there is a prime p with n < p.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- exists_prime_gt 2>/dev/null | grep -qxF 'Nat.exists_prime_gt	3	((x0 : AxNat) -> Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x1 : AxNat) => And (AxNat.lt x0 x1) (And (AxNat.le (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x1) (((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat.dvd x2 x1) -> Or (Eq.{1} AxNat x2 (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (Eq.{1} AxNat x2 x1)))))))'
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type. Euclid's argument, done over N with no subtraction: take m = n! + 1, which is >= 2 because 1 <= n! (`one_le_factorial`), and let q be a prime dividing it (`exists_prime_dvd`). If q <= n then `dvd_factorial_of_le` gives q | n!, and with q | n!+1 `dvd_add_right_cancel_of_pos` yields q | 1, refuted by `not_dvd_one_of_two_le`. So n <= q, and the n = q case falls to the same contradiction after transporting n <= n along the equality, leaving n < q. The command matches the FULL RENDERED TYPE (grep -qxF), not the theorem name: lane `nat-prime-divisor` measured that a name-only checker survives a weakened statement -- spelling a primality bound `1 <= p` instead of `2 <= p` still type-checks, still admits, and is satisfied by p = 1. The kernel cannot see a weaker statement; only the type can.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat prelude's trusted surface is empty
evidence.notes: `theorem_axiom_footprint` reports `nat Nat.exists_prime_gt 0` and `integer Nat.exists_prime_gt 0`. `nat_axiom_inventory` bounds it by enumerating the whole trusted surface: a theorem cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain. Counting `Declaration::Axiom` alone would not suffice -- `Opaque` has no proof body and `Quotient` admits `Quot.sound` -- so all three kinds are covered.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.exists_prime_gt : ((n : AxNat) -> Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (p : AxNat) => And (AxNat.lt n p) (And (AxNat.le (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) p) ((d : AxNat) -> ((hd : AxNat.dvd d p) -> Or (Eq.{1} AxNat d (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (Eq.{1} AxNat d p))))))

Claim.notes: `open` here means NOT ESTABLISHED IN THIS LEDGER; it is not mathematically open, Euclid settled it. It is recorded because it is a live target rather than a curiosity: the prelude already carries `Nat.not_dvd_one_add_mul_of_two_le`, which is exactly the step `no a >= 2 divides 1 + a*t` -- the contradiction at the end of Euclid's argument. 2026-08-17: BOTH missing ingredients have now landed and this fact is one slice from closing. `Nat.factorial` is declared (computation rules definitional, like `Nat.pow`) together with `Nat.dvd_factorial_of_le : (d n : AxNat) -> AxNat.le 1 d -> AxNat.le d n -> AxNat.dvd d (AxNat.factorial n)`, so the number that every positive `d <= n` divides exists in the kernel and `1 + n!` is a witness with no divisor in `[2, n]`. The second ingredient is `F:nat-exists-prime-dvd`: `Nat.exists_prime_dvd : (m : AxNat) -> AxNat.le 2 m -> Exists p, (2 <= p AND forall d, d | p -> d = 1 OR d = p) AND p | m`, admitted axiom-free. Note it did NOT go through `lt_well_founded` as this note previously predicted -- strong induction on `m` would have to DECIDE primality of `m`, a bounded universal quantification whose constructive decision is itself a bounded search, so the search (`Nat.least_divisor_search`) is done directly by ordinary `Nat.rec` on the bound and returns the LEAST divisor >= 2, which is prime for free. WHAT REMAINS is exactly two steps, both small: (1) `1 <= Nat.factorial n` -- factorial is positive, by induction with `one_le_mul` at the successor -- which is what makes `2 <= 1 + n!` and so lets `exists_prime_dvd` be applied to it at all; and (2) the assembly. The assembly: take `p` prime with `p | 1 + n!`; if `p <= n` then `dvd_factorial_of_le` gives `p | n!`, `add_comm` reshapes `1 + n!` to `n! + 1`, `dvd_add_right_cancel_of_pos` yields `p | 1`, and `not_dvd_one_of_two_le` refutes it; so `le_total` leaves `n <= p`, and `lt_or_eq_of_le` turns that into `n < p` once `n = p` is ruled out by the same contradiction. Every lemma named in that paragraph is already admitted axiom-free. formal.statement is written in the SAME core rendering the kernel emits for its own theorems, and uses ONLY symbols `build_nat_prelude` actually declares (checked against the 119-theorem inventory dumped on 2026-08-14), so it can be dispatched without inventing vocabulary. Primality is spelled out inline because the prelude has no `Prime` predicate. Binders carry readable names rather than the kernel's `x0, x1, ...`; that is a pretty-printing difference only, and any admitted proof would render with positional names.

Prose.text: The empty axiom footprint above is the strong claim, not a missing field: `Kernel::axiom_footprint` walked this declaration's transitive dependencies and found no `Axiom`, `Opaque` or `Quotient` in the closure. The schema requires the field when a fact is `proved` precisely so that absence and emptiness cannot be confused.

Claim.label: Bezout's identity holds for the natural gcd
Claim.statement: For all natural numbers m and n there exist natural numbers mp, mn, np, nn with gcd(m, n) + m*mn + n*nn = m*mp + n*np. This is Bezout's identity in balanced form: the usual `gcd(m,n) = m*x + n*y` with integer x, y, rearranged so both sides are natural numbers.

evidence.supports: For all natural numbers m and n there exist natural numbers mp, mn, np, nn with gcd(m, n) + m*mn + n*nn = m*mp + n*np. This is Bezout's identity in balanced form: the usual `gcd(m,n) = m*x + n*y` with integer x, y, rearranged so both sides are natural numbers.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- gcd_bezout 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '^Nat\.gcd_bezout[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type, so producing the row at all is a machine-checked proof. TIGHTENED 2026-08-16: the command was `cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib nat_prelude`, a whole-suite run that passes or fails identically for every fact citing it and would stay green if THIS theorem were deleted. It now names its own subject twice over -- `nat_theorem_inventory` exits non-zero for a name that does not exist, and the `grep -q` requires the admitted declaration to be printed.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat prelude's trusted surface is empty
evidence.notes: `nat_axiom_inventory` enumerates the built Nat environment and reports `nat: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0 total_trusted=0` (re-run 2026-08-14 by this lane). That is the whole environment, not this theorem, and that is what makes it sound as a footprint: a theorem cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain, so an empty trusted surface bounds every individual footprint by []. Counting `Declaration::Axiom` alone would NOT have sufficed -- `Opaque` has no proof body and `Quotient` admits `Quot.sound`, one of Lean's own axioms -- so the enumeration covers all three.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.gcd_bezout : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> AxNat.bezout x0 x1 (AxNat.gcd x0 x1)))

Claim.notes: `AxNat.bezout m n g` abbreviates the balanced form. The balancing is forced: the naturals have no negatives, so a Bezout coefficient that would be negative is moved to the other side of the equation instead. formal.statement is the type the kernel admitted, taken verbatim from Kernel::render_lean over the environment build_nat_prelude produces; it was not transcribed by hand. The sort renders as `AxNat` (the prelude's own inductive) while declarations are rooted at `Nat`.

Claim.label: The four-colour Rado number of 5(x-y) = 3z is 625
Claim.statement: R_4(5(x-y)=3z) = 625. The lower bound is the a-adic valuation colouring of Chang-De Loera-Wesley's Lemma 4.1 (R_k >= a^k), replayed and verified three ways; the upper bound is a refutation at n = 625 with a self-checked DRAT certificate.

evidence.supports: R_4(5(x-y)=3z) = 625, both bounds, with pinned deciding instance and regeneration recipe
evidence.notes: The claim carries the pinned CNF, the replayable lower-bound colouring, and the DRAT regeneration recipe.
Cheap and real: re-verifies the colouring three ways from the stored file in ~0.1s.

evidence.supports: the refutation's verdict names this exact formula
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run --release -q -p axeyum-search --example rado_dump_cnf -- a=5 b=3 k=4 n=625 out=/tmp/rb3.cnf >/dev/null 2>&1; sha256sum /tmp/rb3.cnf | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$(sha256sum artifacts/claims/rado/rado-r4-a5-b3/F_625.cnf | cut -d' ' -f1)"
evidence.notes: Regeneration, not storage comparison: the bytes must come back out of the same encoder.

Claim.notes:
The last blank cell of the a >= b+2 row at a=5, k=4, and the interesting one: b=3 is the LAST cell still INSIDE Chang-De Loera-Wesley's hypothesis (gcd(5,3)=1 and 5 >= 3+2 holds exactly), so 625 = a^4 confirms the k>=4 generalisation where it should hold. b=4 sits outside the hypothesis and breaks to 741, which is consistent rather than contradictory.

The certificate is NOT re-checked per commit -- a 4-hour re-check cannot be a gate -- and the axiom_footprint says so rather than implying the proof is re-derived on every run. The three checkers that DO run are cheap and real: the claim's schema and semantics, the lower-bound colouring replayed from its stored file, and the deciding CNF re-derived from the encoder and compared by hash.

Claim.label: fp8 E5M2 addition under roundNearestTiesToEven is associative
Claim.statement: Let F be the IEEE-754-conformant 8-bit format OCP fp8 E5M2, SMT-LIB `(_ FloatingPoint 5 3)`, and let RNE denote roundNearestTiesToEven. For all values a, b, c of F: fp.add(RNE, fp.add(RNE, a, b), c) equals fp.add(RNE, a, fp.add(RNE, b, c)), where equality is SMT-LIB `=` on the FloatingPoint sort. THIS PROPOSITION IS FALSE. The fact is recorded with status `refuted` and carries a concrete counterexample triple, together with the exact number of triples at which it fails.

evidence.supports: The negation of formal.statement is satisfiable over fp8 E5M2, so the proposition does not hold for all triples.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run --release -q -p axeyum-bench --example smtcomp_cli -- --evidence artifacts/facts/smt2/fp8-add-not-associative.smt2 | tail -1)" = sat
evidence.notes: Ran 2026-08-14: `; evidence kind=sat-model certified=1 recheck=na arena=ok ms=27`, verdict `sat`. `arena=ok` is `Evidence::check` evaluating the produced model against a FRESH PARSE of the original assertions, so the witness is checked against the source formula, not the lowered form. NOT cross-checked by either external oracle, and that is the finding recorded in this fact's notes: neither z3 4.13.3 nor bitwuzla 0.9.1 can decide any fp8 E5M2 addition query at all.

evidence.supports: The specific triple a = b = 0x01 (the E5M2 subnormal 2^-16), c = 0x08 (the normal 2^-13), pinned as a GROUND formula: (a+b)+c = 0x09 while a+(b+c) = 0x08.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run --release -q -p axeyum-bench --example smtcomp_cli -- --evidence artifacts/facts/smt2/fp8-add-not-associative-witness.smt2 | tail -1)" = sat
evidence.notes:
Ran 2026-08-14: `sat`, 2ms. The file has NO free symbols -- it asserts the disequality AND both concrete results -- so a `sat` verdict is direct evaluation of fp8 E5M2 arithmetic rather than a search, and it pins the witness so the fact cannot drift from the solver. Cross-checked: `z3 -smt2` also reports `sat` on this file. That z3 can settle the GROUND instance while returning `unknown` on the quantifier-free SEARCH is not a contradiction: z3's refusal is in its symbolic fpa2bv tactic, and a closed term is constant-folded before that tactic is reached. bitwuzla 0.9.1 refuses the file outright (unsupported format).

Arithmetic, for a reader: a+b = 2^-15 exactly; (a+b)+c = 2^-13 * 1.25 = 0x09 exactly; but b+c = 2^-13 * 1.125 is a tie between 0x08 and 0x09 that RNE breaks toward the even significand, giving 0x08, and a + 0x08 ties again to 0x08. Two ties in one direction is what separates the two bracketings.

evidence.supports: All 2^24 = 16777216 fp8 E5M2 triples enumerated by LLVM's APFloat: the two bracketings disagree at 427036 of them under RNE (2.55%).
evidence.notes: Ran 2026-08-14, 2.2s. Independent of axeyum's bit-blaster, CNF encoder and SAT core: `rustc_apfloat` 0.2.3 (LLVM APFloat), comparing SMT-LIB value classes. The failure count is mode-dependent and was measured for all five SMT-LIB rounding modes: RNE 427036, RNA 419652, RTP 4825040, RTN 4825040, RTZ 5375600 -- of 16777216 triples each. The directed modes fail an order of magnitude more often, and RTP/RTN fail equally often, which is the sign symmetry of the format. The first witness in enumeration order is the same triple under every mode. The binary exits non-zero if the claim ever stops failing.

formal.statement: (assert (= (fp.add RNE (fp.add RNE a b) c) (fp.add RNE a (fp.add RNE b c))))

Claim.notes:
WHY A REFUTATION IS THE VALUABLE RESULT HERE. Every reduction kernel, every tensor-parallel all-reduce and every reordering optimizer relies on being allowed to re-bracket a sum. This fact says precisely how often that is wrong at fp8 E5M2: 427036 of 16777216 triples under RNE, and 5375600 -- nearly a third -- under round-toward-zero. That is a measured density with a named witness, not an aphorism.

THE FINDING ABOUT THE ORACLES. This claim could not be cross-checked against either industrial FP solver, for two DIFFERENT reasons, and both were measured on 2026-08-14 rather than assumed:
  * z3 4.13.3 returns `unknown` with `(:reason-unknown "addition/subtract with ebits > sbits not supported")`. E5M2 has 5 exponent bits and 3 significand bits, so every fp8 addition query is outside its fpa2bv tactic.
  * bitwuzla 0.9.1 errors out: "Unsupported experimental floating-point format (non-experimental: Float16, Float32, Float64, Float128)". The `--fpexp` escape named in that message is a BUILD option, not a runtime flag -- passing it to the binary is rejected as an invalid option, so this build cannot be talked into it.
So at exactly the width where a claim can be settled by brute force, the two solvers a practitioner would reach for decline. axeyum decides it, and the LLVM-APFloat enumeration is what independently confirms the answer. Note the complementary gap in the other direction: axeyum REFUSES fp8 E4M3, correctly, because E4M3 has no infinities and an all-ones NaN and is therefore not an IEEE format -- `arithmetic_format_supported` gates it out, while z3 accepts (_ FloatingPoint 4 4) happily.

ROUTE. `search-certificate`: the settlement is a replayable witness, matching the precedent of F:affirming-the-consequent. Refuting a universally quantified claim costs one triple; establishing one costs the whole space -- and here we paid both, because the enumeration also gives the density.

Steps.heading: The argument for the bottom node
Steps.caption: This block carries **no provenance**, which is the schema's signal that a person wrote it: it is the human argument, not a captured machine trace. The machine's version of it is the proof term the kernel checked, and the card above is where that is recorded.

steps.note: Any prime dividing N is larger than n, if one exists.

steps.output: N has a prime divisor p
steps.note: This is `F:nat-exists-prime-dvd`, one layer up in the graph.
p is one of the factors of n!.
This is `F:nat-dvd-add`, which is why that node is an ancestor of this one and not merely nearby.

Prose.heading: What this file is
Prose.text: One file. The stylesheet, the script, both figures and every glyph are inside it, and opening it makes no network request -- a property checked by `lint_self_contained`, which has a unit test per violation class so that it can actually fail. Print it and the reading-level control disappears, every fold opens, and the badges stay distinguishable because each one carries a shape as well as a colour.
